original_card.question: Can a new local cost interface change the deficit-to-recursive-cost ratio beyond current packing?
methods: Propose a changed helper inventory and derive an optimistic exact moment.
Design a small completed instance and independently verify its endpoint and rank bill.
original_card.acceptance_gate: A new physically realizable contract outside the frozen catalogue whose per-call profile, screened with ceiling.ceiling(), beats the selected word's packing ceiling; a lower cap does not establish identical circuitry or order attainable optima, and is insufficient to pass the stronger-budget target under this model. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Read the selected word's per-call local profile, its packing ceiling and the lever table; run levers.py for the ideal budget of the lever you target.
first_step.scope: Positive control and planning budget only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Before any synthesis, write the candidate per-call local profile (and centre charge / unpaid coordinates if changed) and screen it with ceiling.ceiling(); reject it if even the ideal ceiling does not beat the selected word's by your stated margin.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Packing of the selected word is capped at +0.87% (ceiling model); only a lower local excess spend or a changed coverage law raises the cap.
allowed_variations: Narrow to one changed boundary or helper type with explicit counts.
If the coverage law, template or guard changes, derive an applicable fully charged replacement bound instead of applying the incumbent ceiling outside its scope.
scope_change_triggers: Mixing only providers already inside the pinned catalogue.
Only changing helper terminal subspaces and monotone frames within the fixed scalar word, entrances and cleanup contract already covered by #1995/#2013.

Continuing a partial cost improvement while leaving the same unpriced consumer, restoration or central-readout obligation unresolved; refresh the family expansion decision first. Local product-retiming evidence has a narrow scope and is not a ban on changed graphs or contracts.

actual_scope: On both pinned PR2979 orientations, pool observations from incomparable rank-seven terminal subspaces; extend the complete pair/triple census to all four-class supports, screen them over GF(3), and exactly recheck every rank-defect candidate over Q for sparse eligible input readouts.
scope_change_reason: The pair/triple census exposed a five-dimensional block, but its known basis uses six- and eight-coordinate forms. This bounded follow-up tests a changed premise that could make a caller-facing interface cheaper: whether four endpoint classes yield a sparse basis without materializing their rank-nine join. It remains a linear-information experiment; the family cost gate forbids a construction campaign until one real caller and its complete transfer budget are identified.
bottleneck_link: Six sparse quartet readouts add a five-dimensional basis, with four five-coordinate forms, but no product caller or physical realization is established. A kappa change requires a named caller, fully charged observation, storage, restoration and recursive costs; the >0.01 target also needs both effective supplier budgets above 1/99.
stop_rule: Check all 49 choose 4 endpoint-class supports on both pinned orientations, using GF(3) only as a complete candidate screen and exact rational arithmetic for every candidate. Stop before synthesis unless a real caller consumes the sparse block and the complete boundary/cost ledger leaves a plausible route through the family expansion gate.
evidence: verify.py independently reconstructs both pinned PR2979 words and exact formal-warp adjoints. It checks all singleton classes, 1,176 pairs, 18,424 triples and 211,876 four-class supports. For quartets, the nine-dimensional protected kernel gives a complete GF(3) screen: 1,353 candidates all have rank-nine joins and are rechecked exactly over Q; their eligible-rank histogram is 1:1,258, 2:94, 3:1. The quartet census adds six exact forms (four five-term, one eight-term, one ten-term) spanning the same five-space; six selected identities use nine terminal registers across seven rank-seven endpoint classes. Both orientations agree. All protected input columns and nonempty warp words cancel. No caller, complete invoice or kappa improvement is established.
author: OpenAI Codex
ai_assistance: Substantial OpenAI Codex assistance for the research direction, exact checker, computation and documentation. No independent human review is claimed.

open_questions.question: Does any actual downstream call consume the six-form sparse block, or its five-dimensional span?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The sparse equations are only useful if they replace recursive work that the caller already needs; observing them alone has no kappa value.
open_questions.first_step: Trace each h-coordinate into one named producer/consumer boundary, identify the required subspace of forms, and compare it with the span of all six identities (the four five-term forms alone span only three dimensions).
open_questions.blocked_by: No matching caller or source-to-consumer contract has been identified.

open_questions.question: Can the seven-endpoint, nine-register observation be implemented and paid below the rank-nine transfer allowance?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The endpoints have a rank-nine join, so separately pricing or materializing a shared rank-nine helper could erase all savings.
open_questions.first_step: For the matched caller, derive a direct multi-register circuit, dirty-state restoration, chronology, storage and exact recursive profile; apply the family expansion gate before further search.
open_questions.blocked_by: No complete physical, restoration or recursive invoice exists; selected kappa is unchanged.
